opportunities.title: registerUser access token can reference a different user id
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `registerUser()` currently builds the returned `id` and the JWT `sub` with two separate `Date.now()` calls. If time advances between those calls, the API can return one user id while signing an access token for a different subject. Downstream authenticated requests would then identify a different user than the one returned by registration. ## Expected fix Generate the new user id once, return that id, and sign the access token with the same id as `sub`. Add a regression test that forces the timestamp to advance between calls and verifies the token subject matches the returned id. ## Scope This issue is limited to the registration response/token subject mismatch in `apps/api/src/services/authService.js` plus focused API service test coverage. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information. References #743.

opportunities.title: check_correctness / lcb_check_correctness_v2 leave a zombie process after killing a timed-out test run
opportunities.summary: ## Description `check_correctness` (`rllm/rewards/code_reward.py:120`) and `lcb_check_correctness_v2` (line 231) run untrusted generated code in a `multiprocessing.Process`, and on timeout do `if process.is_alive(): process.kill()` with no `process.join()` after it. `kill()` only delivers SIGKILL; the child isn't reaped until something calls `join()`/`wait()` on it, so it sits as a zombie (`STAT=Z`) for the life of the worker process. `lcb_check_correctness_v2` runs on every code-task reward through `RewardCodeFn.__call__` (the LiveCodeBench path and the default fallback), so any slow or hanging generation during RL training leaks one zombie per timeout on that worker. Each one is harmless alone, but a long run with many workers and timeouts can eventually hit the OS per-user PID limit. ## Steps to Reproduce Call `check_correctness` with a `test_fn` that sleeps past `timeout_per_test`, then check for the spawned child: ```python import os, subprocess, time from rllm.rewards.code_reward import check_correctness def test_fn(*a, **k): time.sleep(30) check_correctness({"inputs": ["1"], "outputs": ["1"]}, "x = 1", test_fn, timeout_per_test=2, max_tests=15) time.sleep(1) print(subprocess
